clue.text: Disturbed night — drug please!

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters of the next three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insomniac, up after a restless night, begs for something to knock them out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: 'Disturbed' shuffles NIGHT, DRUG and PLEASE, and the sleepless person's plea describes what they want.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea for medication after a broken night is exactly a request for a sedative drink taken to bring on sleep.

clue.text: Transport taking 50 people up?

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle for hire, a form of transport
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A vehicle carrying fifty passengers up a mountainside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a cab 'taking' L and an upturned RACE is what carries people up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin hauled on an overhead wire is mountain transport that lifts its passengers uphill.

clue.text: Design phase botched

indicators.note: something botched is messed up, so the letters of phase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A designer admits one stage of the project went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Design as a noun means form or outline, which is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Confined to bed at this point, not primarily making sense

indicators.note: something confined to a bed is held inside it, so the next pieces go inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
at this point means here

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of not is used

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in bed right now is not mainly talking sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confined to bed' reads like an invalid's state, but it is a container instruction; 'not primarily' gives just N.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherent speech is logical and consistent, so it is speech making sense.

clue.text: Not doing as much in class?

definitions.text: Not doing as much in class?

parts.words: Not doing as much in class?
parts.note: split as two words, the clue's phrase becomes '...', having less going on, while the whole is a period of teaching in a class

explanation.surface: A pupil slacking off at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as LESS ON, the answer means having less going on; read whole, it is a period of teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a single teaching period at school, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Delayed start for hostilities — bad weather combination brings ceasefire

indicators.note: a start that is delayed has not arrived yet, so the opening letter of the word for hostilities is missing

parts.note: war is armed hostilities
two kinds of bad weather put together: mist and ice

explanation.surface: Fighting gets off to a late start and fog plus frost lead to a truce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delayed start for' drops the W of WAR, leaving AR.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a formal agreement to stop fighting, a synonym of ceasefire.

clue.text: Stick heard shattering — ultimately brittle

indicators.note: shattering breaks something into pieces, so the letters of heard are rearranged
ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of brittle is used

explanation.surface: Someone hears a brittle stick snap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like the twig that broke, but it is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to something is to cling or attach firmly, a synonym.

clue.text: Guidelines here laid down for moderate

definitions.meaning: the white lines painted on a carriageway are laid along its centre
moderate means avoiding extremes, especially in politics

explanation.surface: Rules set out for a moderate person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guidelines' is literal: painted lines guiding traffic along the centre of a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrist view sits between the extremes, the idiomatic sense of moderate.

clue.text: Look in to restrain son being obnoxious

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the word for in holds the letter for son inside

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'is she in?'

explanation.surface: A parent checks on a son being kept in for behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link word: it means AT HOME, which holds S.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome and obnoxious both mean causing disgust or strong dislike.

clue.text: Almost set one, maybe two bones?

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a radio is a receiving set
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone nearly setting a broken limb with two bones in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' suggests setting a bone, but it is a radio set.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone; its plural can describe two of them, one in each arm, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Solar event in these clips examined

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Scientists study film footage of the sun being blotted out.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon blocks the sun's light from earth, that solar event has this name.

clue.text: Gratuity in post used as wage

indicators.note: in places the tip word inside the word for post

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a tip is a gratuity

explanation.surface: A tip received in the mail treated as pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a job or the mail as a noun; it is the verb SEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular payment such as a salary, a synonym of wage.

clue.text: Winger losing front part of foot

indicators.note: losing its front means the bird's first letter is removed

parts.note: a winger is something with wings, here a bird such as a finch

explanation.surface: A wide player loses part of a foot, perhaps in a football injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests football; it is a bird. 'foot' is a unit of length, of which this is a twelfth.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot as a measure is divided into twelve of these smaller imperial units.

clue.text: Showing one's support for movie with Sellers

definitions.meaning: turning up for someone in a time of need
a 1979 film starring Peter Sellers as the gardener Chance

explanation.surface: A fan demonstrates their loyalty to a Sellers film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sellers' looks like traders but is the actor Peter Sellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporting someone often means simply turning up in person; the phrase is also a famous film title.

clue.text: Cast made moral sentiment the focus here?

indicators.note: to cast is to mould into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cast of actors makes a moral point, with emotion at the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests actors, fitting the stage scene, but it shuffles MADE MORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A play built on heightened emotion and sentimentality rather than subtlety is a sensational stage genre.

clue.text: Man respected concealing weapon in coat?

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the weapon goes inside the word for man

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a respected man
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A respectable man hides a gun inside his overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat is one example of an item of clothing, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Give ground with defender shown red card?

parts.note: a back is a defender in football
a player shown a red card is sent off

explanation.surface: A football defender is dismissed and the team must retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: To give ground is to retreat or withdraw, which the phrasal verb means.

clue.text: I'm loaded, but money's stolen

parts.note: bucks are dollars, money
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A rich person boasts, but the cash was stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' suggests wealth, but the answer is what is loaded into a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot is ammunition loaded into a shotgun cartridge, so it can say this of itself.

clue.text: Supremo for D-Day operation?

definitions.meaning: a supremo is a supreme ruler or boss
the codename for the Allied invasion of Normandy in 1944

explanation.surface: Choosing a commander for the Normandy landings.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme lord ruling over others is a supremo; the same word codenamed the 1944 invasion.

clue.text: Review top secret revenue's source after hacking

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter
after being hacked into and chopped about, the letters of top secret are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tax office reviews its classified files after a cyberattack.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking back over past events is a review, an idiomatic sense of the answer as in 'in hindsight'.

clue.text: Those from royal house built in Stroud

indicators.note: something built is assembled from parts, so the letters of Stroud are put together anew

explanation.surface: Royals whose house was built in Stroud, a town in Gloucestershire, England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal house' and 'built' suggest a building; the house is a dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The family of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I were members of this English royal house.

clue.text: On time to assist an erring actor?

definitions.meaning: to remind an actor who has forgotten a line by whispering it

explanation.surface: Being punctual in order to help an actor who fluffs lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Punctual means on time; a stage helper also feeds forgotten lines, the verb sense.

clue.text: Certain notes hard to harmonise

parts.note: me (or mi) is a note in the sol-fa scale, so certain notes are mes
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Some musical notes are difficult to fit into harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that fit together well are said to mesh, like interlocking gears, so it means harmonise.

clue.text: Stop at sea: the Spanish brought into harbour

indicators.note: brought into means put inside, so the Spanish article goes into the harbour word

parts.note: a bay is a sheltered inlet, a harbour
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish ship is brought into port to stop sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Belay is a nautical command meaning stop, so it means stop at sea.

clue.text: Open about amount of work experience

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for open goes around the unit of work

parts.note: to undo something is to open it
an erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Starting work experience with a vague idea of the workload.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or go through it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Immense rook goes after girl

indicators.note: goes after means the rook letter follows the girl's name

parts.note: Stella is a girl's name
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A huge rook chases a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar means outstanding or huge, as in 'stellar growth', synonymous with immense.

clue.text: Runner on form perhaps marks female group

parts.note: a hare is a fast runner that rests in a form, its grassy hollow
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An athlete in good form picks up points with a group of women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on form' suggests an athlete playing well; a form is a hare's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The women of a household in some traditional societies make up a harem, a female group.

clue.text: Support the courts for your country

parts.note: a prop is a support
atria are open courtyards in Roman houses, plural of atrium

explanation.surface: Supporting the national courts out of patriotism.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase translates as on behalf of the fatherland, a patriotic motto.
